heroHeadline: Xiang Yang Hong 33 Day 22 Near Pag-asa; UNCLOS Note Verbale Silence Day 17 — Longest Unanswered Philippine Diplomatic Instrument Under Marcos; AUKUS Under Parliamentary Scrutiny as UK Report Calls Program 'Inadequate, Losing Credibility'
heroSubtitle: China's research vessel Xiang Yang Hong 33, escorted by CCG vessels 5101 and 5309, maintained its unauthorized presence in the Kalayaan Island Group near Pag-asa (Thitu) Island for a 22nd consecutive day on May 28, 2026, as Beijing's diplomatic silence on the Philippines' UNCLOS Article 246 note verbale extended to a 17th consecutive day — cementing its status as the longest unanswered Philippine diplomatic instrument under the Marcos administration. The Philippines' three-front West Philippine Sea standoff persisted with no kinetic escalation: (1) Xiang Yang Hong 33 near Pag-asa (Day 22; PCG Sandy Cay 2/3 personnel landing investigation ongoing; UNCLOS Art. 246 note verbale silence Day 17); (2) Scarborough Shoal — DFA protest of China's 'marine nature reserve' declaration unanswered; AFP weekly report confirmed 19 Chinese vessels (10 PLAN + 9 CCG) for May 19-25 — highest 2026 concentration; (3) Second Thomas Shoal — BRP Sierra Madre garrison facing CCG blockade posture (1 PLAN + 8 CCG). AFP's weekly WPS count: 36 Chinese vessels across four features for May 19-25, up 33% from 27 the prior week. In the AUKUS dimension, May 2026 brought mounting institutional scrutiny: a UK Parliament Intelligence and Security Committee report called AUKUS defense trade cooperation 'so far inadequate' and warned the program is 'rapidly losing credibility,' while former Australian PM Malcolm Turnbull told Chatham House the deal represented 'a huge wealth transfer from the Australian government to the US and the UK' — with submarines years away and the domestic-build promise uncertain. All three AUKUS partner governments reaffirmed commitment at official levels. PCG continued aerial surveillance against the Xiang Yang Hong 33; no new kinetic incidents confirmed.
